cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: The control plane is the brain of the cluster: kube-apiserver, etcd, kube-scheduler and kube-controller-manager. Together they accept requests, store desired state, make scheduling decisions and keep the cluster running the way users declared it.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: The core idea is reconciliation: controllers keep comparing desired state with actual state and fix any difference. Worker nodes form a separate data plane that only talks to the control plane through kube-apiserver, so running Pods keep working if the control plane is briefly down.

questions.q: Name the four core control-plane components.
If the control plane goes down, do running apps stop?
questions.a: No. Already-running Pods keep running because kubelet, kube-proxy and the container runtime on each node do not need the control plane every second. You just cannot make changes or self-heal until it returns.

questions.q: What does reconciliation mean in Kubernetes?
questions.a: Controllers continuously compare the desired state stored in etcd with the actual cluster state and take action until they match.
